Forecast with a Timestral model through predict()

Source: R/forecaster.R
predict.timestral_model.Rd

The stats::predict() interface to timestral_forecast(). Timestral is a zero-shot model, so there is nothing fitted to predict from: newdata is the series to forecast (the context), not new predictor values.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'timestral_model'
predict(object, newdata, h, ...)

Arguments

object

a timestral_model from timestral_load()

newdata

the series to forecast; anything timestral_forecast() accepts as y

h

horizon in steps (required)

...

further arguments to timestral_forecast(), such as covariates, observation_mask or symmetric

Value

A timestral_forecast, exactly as from timestral_forecast(); use timestral_median() or timestral_quantile() for point values.

Examples

m <- timestral_load(system.file("extdata", "tiny", package = "timestralR"))
fc <- predict(m, AirPassengers, h = 12)
timestral_median(fc)
#>           Jan      Feb      Mar      Apr      May      Jun      Jul      Aug
#> 1961 291.3287 360.7115 280.6464 318.2002 223.7060 189.5016 350.5766 244.7158
#>           Sep      Oct      Nov      Dec
#> 1961 270.5898 313.5198 281.9475 301.3957
